overview.description: DESYNC is a leader-worker consensus protocol for blockchain sequencing, using epochs for leadership rotation, VRF-based elections, PoS staking, and optimistic execution with fraud proofs. Leaders order transactions deterministically, workers execute in parallel with state synchronization, leader bundles to L1. Supports dynamic node joining after cluster initialization, processed at epoch boundaries.

voted_hash_commit.description: Committed VRF hash (null if not committed).

revealed_hash.description: Revealed VRF hash (0 if not revealed).

genesis_config.description: Genesis configuration for new cluster initialization.

cluster_members.description: Initial set of nodes with IDs, addresses, public keys, and stakes.

genesis_timestamp.description: Microsecond timestamp for starting the first epoch.

minimum_stake.description: Minimum stake required for election participation.

total_stake.description: Sum of all initial stakes for quorum checks.

epoch_duration.description: Duration of each epoch (must match constants.epoch_duration).

bootstrap_nodes.description: List of trusted node addresses (hostname:port) for new nodes to contact for leader discovery and cluster joining.

log.description: Replicated log of ordered transactions with state transitions.

backup_leader_id.description: Current backup leader ID (null if unknown).

last_heartbeat.description: Last heartbeat from leader and backup leader.

batch_sequence.description: Next batch sequence number for ordering.

pending_join_requests.description: Pending node join requests awaiting approval at epoch boundary.

arrival_timestamp.description: Microsecond timestamp when received by leader.

signature.description: Signature of node_id || address || public_key || stake.

vrf_generate_hash.signature: vrfGenerateHash(seed: byte_array, private_key: byte_array) -> (hash: uint64, proof: byte_array)
vrf_generate_hash.description: Generates verifiable random hash and proof.

vrf_verify_hash.signature: vrfVerifyHash(hash: uint64, proof: byte_array, public_key: byte_array, seed: byte_array) -> boolean
vrf_verify_hash.description: Verifies VRF hash was generated correctly.

determine_leaders.signature: determineLeaders(revealed_hashes: map[node_id: (uint64, uint64)]) -> (leader_id: uint64, backup_id: uint64)
determine_leaders.description: Stakes-weighted selection: lowest weighted_hash = leader, second = backup. weighted_hash = hash / stake.

poh_verify_time.description: Verifies PoH tick chain confirms time passage.

compute_state_root.description: Computes merkle root of state after applying changes.

verify_execution.signature: verifyExecution(tx: Transaction, result: ExecutionResult, proof: byte_array) -> boolean
verify_execution.description: Verifies execution result using merkle proof.

compute_epoch_seed.signature: computeEpochSeed(epoch: uint64, genesis_timestamp: uint64 | null) -> byte_array
compute_epoch_seed.description: Computes epoch seed. For epoch 1, uses sha256(genesis_timestamp || epoch); otherwise, uses PoH-based seed.

verify_join_signature.description: Verifies the signature of a node join request.

accept_transaction.description: Leader only: Receives transaction, assigns ID, records arrival timestamp with microsecond precision.

order_transactions_deterministic.description: Leader only: Orders transactions by (arrival_timestamp, tx_id) for deterministic ordering despite clock skew.

create_sequential_batches.description: Leader only: Splits transactions into sequential batches (1-100 to worker1, 101-200 to worker2, etc.).

execute_batch_with_dependencies.description: Worker only: Executes batch, requests state dependencies if needed, signs results with execution proof.

request_state_dependency.description: Worker only: Requests state from another worker for dependency resolution.

resolve_execution_conflicts.description: Leader only: Orders batch results by sequence number, applies state changes sequentially.

bundle_to_l1.description: Leader only: Creates rollup bundle with ordered transactions and state root for L1 submission.

submit_fraud_proof.signature: submitFraudProof(disputed_tx_id: byte_array, correct_result: ExecutionResult, proof: byte_array)
submit_fraud_proof.description: Any node: Submits fraud proof with correct execution result and merkle proof.

validate_fraud_proof.description: Validates fraud proof by re-executing transaction and comparing results.

emergency_election.description: Triggers emergency election when both leader and backup are unresponsive.

slash_stake.signature: slashStake(node_id: uint64, violation_type: string, evidence: byte_array)
slash_stake.description: Slashes stake for violations: non_participation, false_execution, unresponsive.

query_cluster_for_leader.signature: queryClusterForLeader() -> (leader_id: uint64, backup_leader_id: uint64, epoch: uint64)
query_cluster_for_leader.description: Queries cluster members to discover current leader, backup leader, and epoch.

request_node_join.signature: requestNodeJoin(node_id: uint64, address: string, public_key: byte_array, stake: uint64, signature: byte_array) -> boolean
request_node_join.description: New node requests to join the cluster; sent to leader for validation and approval.

validate_node_join.description: Leader and workers validate a node join request; requires 2/3 stake approval.

process_pending_joins.description: Leader only: Processes pending join requests at epoch boundary after election.

total_stake.description: Updated total stake of the cluster.

all_nodes: Maintain role based on election results
Use PoH to verify epoch timing and transitions
Participate in elections if staked (>= minimum_stake)
Monitor heartbeats: leader and backup must send every 100ms
Trigger emergency election if both leader and backup silent for >1s
Apply log entries sequentially: if commit_index > last_applied, apply next entry
Maintain cluster membership and stake tracking
node_initialization: Always start as 'worker' (regardless of previous role)
If genesis_config exists and current_epoch = 0 and current_time >= genesis_timestamp: initiate election for epoch 1 with staggered delay (node_id % 100ms)
If no genesis_config or current_epoch > 0: query cluster for current leader and epoch, initiate join process if in processing phase, or participate in election if in election phase
Start heartbeat timer (100ms) only if elected as leader or backup leader
Verify quorum (>= 2/3 stake) before proceeding with genesis election, retry after genesis_quorum_timeout (10s) if quorum not met
node_joining: New node contacts bootstrap_nodes to query current leader using query_cluster_for_leader
New node sends node_join_request to leader with node_id, address, public_key, stake, and signature
Leader queues node_join_request in pending_join_requests and processes only at epoch boundary after election
Leader verifies stake (>= minimum_stake) and signature, broadcasts node_join_request to cluster for approval
Cluster members validate join request and respond with node_join_approval (2/3 stake approval required)
Leader broadcasts cluster_member_update at start of next epoch’s processing phase, adding new node to cluster_members
New node syncs state with leader and becomes active as worker at next epoch boundary
Limit join requests to one per node per epoch to prevent spam
If leader fails during join, new node retries with backup leader after node_join_timeout (10s)
workers: Receive batch assignments via direct message from leader
Execute batches deterministically using local state snapshot
Request state dependencies from other workers if conflicts detected
Sign execution results with merkle proof of state transitions
Return results to leader within execution timeout (30s)
Monitor leader/backup heartbeats, participate in emergency elections
election_participants: Commit VRF hash during first 40s of election phase
Reveal hash and proof during next 20s
Verify other nodes' reveals using vrf_verify_hash
Calculate weighted hashes: hash / stake for fair selection
Accept leader (lowest weighted hash) and backup (second lowest)
For epoch 1, use genesis_timestamp to compute epoch seed
leaders: Accept transactions with microsecond timestamp precision
Create sequential batches distributed across workers
Send batch assignments via direct messages
Collect signed execution results from workers
Resolve conflicts by applying batch results in sequence order
Bundle finalized transactions to L1 with state root
Send heartbeats every 100ms to all nodes
Claim proportional fees from processed transactions
Handoff state to new leader at epoch boundary
Queue node_join_requests and process at epoch boundary after election, coordinate approval
backup_leaders: Mirror leader's transaction pool and batch state
Ready to take over immediately if leader fails
Monitor leader heartbeats and transaction flow

mev_resistance.fair_ordering: Deterministic ordering by arrival timestamp prevents leader manipulation
mev_resistance.commit_reveal_batching: Future enhancement: leaders commit to batch ordering before seeing all transactions
mev_resistance.fee_distribution: Leaders claim proportional fees, not full MEV extraction
mev_resistance.rotation_frequency: 3-minute epochs limit any single leader's MEV extraction window

fault_tolerance.byzantine_model: Assumes <= 1/3 Byzantine nodes in total cluster
fault_tolerance.leader_failure: Backup takes over immediately, no election needed
fault_tolerance.dual_failure: Emergency election with 1s delay if both leader and backup fail
fault_tolerance.network_partitions: Majority partition continues, minority partitions halt
fault_tolerance.state_inconsistency: Fraud proofs allow challenges to incorrect execution
fault_tolerance.crash_recovery: Restart as 'worker', reload persistent state, sync with current leader, participate in next election if desired, never assumes previous leadership role
fault_tolerance.clock_synchronization: PoH provides common time reference, microsecond timestamps handle skew
fault_tolerance.node_join_failure: If leader fails during join, new node retries with backup leader; unapproved nodes retry in next epoch

fraud_proof_system.dispute_window: 24 hours to challenge any execution result
fraud_proof_system.proof_requirements: Must provide correct execution result with merkle proof
fraud_proof_system.validation_process: Any node can validate by re-executing disputed transaction
fraud_proof_system.penalties: 25% stake slashing for proven false execution
fraud_proof_system.incentives: Successful challengers receive portion of slashed stake

phase_1_mvp: Genesis configuration loading and initial election
Basic node joining with leader validation and epoch-boundary processing
phase_3_production: Optimized node joining with L1 stake verification

security_considerations.sybil_resistance: PoS staking requirement + VRF prevents identity manipulation
security_considerations.election_manipulation: VRF commit-reveal + stake weighting prevents hash grinding
security_considerations.execution_integrity: Signed results + fraud proofs ensure correctness
security_considerations.availability: Backup leader + emergency elections ensure liveness
security_considerations.censorship_resistance: Short epochs + deterministic ordering limit censorship window
security_considerations.genesis_security: Genesis configuration must be securely distributed and verified (e.g., via L1 contract or trusted setup)
security_considerations.node_join_security: Require 2/3 stake approval and signed join requests at epoch boundaries to prevent malicious joins
